newsitem.title: UK: LME probes higher, copper corrects after fall.
newsitem.headline: LME probes higher, copper corrects after fall.

text.p: Base metal prices steadied during early Thursday trading, as copper in particular tried to consolidate and correct after the big sell-off seen this week.

Traders said business was generally ticking over, and conditions would likely remain slow until the official rings. Stock data was mixed, showing increases for copper, tin, lead, and zinc, but drawdowns for the other metals.
"There is not really much going...there is a bit of buying, if only because it (the decline) was a bit overdone," one trader said.

Copper prices continued to foray upwards from Wednesday's 4-1/2 month lows of $2,230, with business this morning ranging from $2,250 to $2,272, up $36 from the overnight kerb close. The cash/threes spread was at $115/120.
However, another rise in stocks - by 2,000 tonnes - and expectations of further significant increases are likely to inhibit advances.
"I think the rallies in copper are going to be sold into," another trader said.
Aluminium ranged up from early little-changed levels to $1,578, up $10 from Wednesday. Stocks dropped by 1,975 tonnes, and IPAI May producer data due at 1000 GMT may show a decline also, some said.
Lead advanced to $664, up $14, with some early short-covering inducing mixed follow-through buying. The market's chart target is around $675.
Zinc also moved higher, and is on course to re-challenge last week's 6-3/4 year highs of $1,495 and the $1,500 level. Prices were $12 higher at $1,484.
Nickel was helped by a stock decline as well, and stood $50 higher at $6,940. Tin gained $10 at $5,520, with the market continuing to be supported just above last week's 2-1/4 year lows.
